items.title: Production deploys are blue/green
items.body: Every production deploy starts a complete new stack next to the running one. Traffic moves only after its health checks pass, and the old stack stays warm for 30 minutes so a rollback is a traffic switch, not a rebuild.

items.title: The job that ran twice
items.question: A billing job on the Acme job queue charged a customer twice after a worker was restarted mid-job. The queue guarantees at-least-once delivery. What should the job handler do so a redelivery is harmless?
items.answer: Make the handler idempotent. Store an idempotency key (for example the job id) with the charge in the same transaction, and skip the work when the key already exists. At-least-once delivery means any job can be redelivered after a crash, so side effects must be safe to repeat.

items.title: Why config is read at startup only
items.question: Why do Acme services read their configuration only at startup instead of watching the config store for changes?
items.answer: A restart turns every config change into a normal, observable rollout: it goes through health checks and can be rolled back like code. Hot reloading would let a bad value reach every instance at once, with no deploy record to point at.
